content:
Maria: kicking off validation for the new on-prem VPC cluster in eu-west-3 — focusing on GPU capacity acceptance, network handoff, and cost tradeoffs 
Jay: good call, thanks. what's the acceptance checklist look like?
Maria: short list: 1) seed registry reachable via mirror, 2) nodes report GPUs and correct drivers, 3) pods can pull offline images, 4) customer BGP + route acceptance, 5) load test to confirm sustained throughput at target SLOs
Priya: for the BGP piece, customer requires we avoid advertising /24s; we'll use /28s from their edge. confirm team has the ASNs and the route-filter template.
Jonah: we have ASN 65030 from the handoff doc, route-filter template attached in the delivery pack. also need to confirm firewall allows GRE+ESP for the IPSec tunnel.
Tomas: quick GPU validation commands I ran:
```
# check driver + cards
kubectl -n kube-system exec -it gpu-node-0 -- nvidia-smi -L
# check device plugin
kubectl get pods -n kube-system -l k8s-app=nvidia-device-plugin
# check DCGM exporter
kubectl top node | grep gpu-node
```
Maria: output looked good on node-0/1/2, all 4xA100s present. DCGM metrics show expected memory and SM usage during the microbench.
Jay: what's the plan for air-gapped image sync? customer won't allow outbound to dockerhub.
Maria: we did a registry seal: mirror-sync tool -> tarball -> scp to customer seed host -> `ctr images import` on the registry VM. Verified with `crane ls` and checksum.
Priya: firewall rules required: outbound to our config IPs 10.10.0.5:5000 (registry), NTP to 169.254.169.123 (internal), and customer CIDR e.g., 172.31.0.0/16 for management. Also opened 2379,2380 (etcd) only on control-plane mgmt subnet.
Tomas: found one flakey node where kubelet was hitting OOM because kube-reserved wasn't set for GPU memory overhead. Patch applied: set kube-reserved.cpu=200m, kube-reserved.memory=1Gi, system-reserved.memory=512Mi, and restarted kubelet. Node stabilized.
Jonah: cost discussion: customer asked about tradeoffs between reserved vs burst GPUs. Our recommendation: start with 75% reserved, 25% burst-on-demand for peak. Rationale: predictable baseline pricing + headroom without long commit.
Maria: we modeled unit economics: baseline reserved pool 12 A100s @ $X/day vs bursting to 18 for peak. At 75% steady utilization, per-inference token cost drops ~18% due to better batching.
Jay: any constraints on region egress costs? eu-west-3 has higher cross-AZ egress; we recommended colocating model artifacts in local registry to avoid repeated pulls.
Priya: also flagged MTU mismatch on the customer's firewall — had to lower node MTU to 1450 for IPsec. Note: if using jumbo frames downstream, coordinate with customer net team.
Maria: validation tests run: 1) 1h soak at 60% baseline load, 2) spike test to simulate 3x QPS for 10m, 3) failover: simulate control-plane master reboot. All passed except kube-scheduler latency spike during node GC window (observed ~420ms).
Tomas: scheduler latency spike traced to I/O contention from logrotate + containerd GC. Mitigation: stagger logrotate and bump containerd gc thresholds. Re-ran spike; scheduler latencies back <200ms.
Jonah: handoff checklist to customer success: 
- confirm ASN + route filters done
- registry tarball checksum + import validated
- firewall rule screenshot + MTU setting confirmed
- reserved vs burst plan signed off (billing contact cc'd)
Maria: I'm attaching the final acceptance artifact (hash: sha256:abcdef...) and the load test graphs to the delivery bundle. Can someone trigger the final deploy job?
deploy-bot: deploy/job 2024-09-12-2145 triggered by Maria — running canary rollout to nodepool-gpu-reserved (3 -> 12)
Jay: watching logs, will comment if anything weird. :eyes:
Priya: FYI customer asked about plugin for kernel modules (nv_peer_mem). We built and signed the module on their host image during provisioning; verify with `lsmod | grep nv_peer_mem`.
Tomas: final note: record we enabled node labels `redwood/gpu-type=a100`, `redwood/billing-tier=reserved` and taints `gpu-only:NoSchedule`. This helps autoscaler and cost accounting.
Jonah: handed off to CS (cc @Sophie-CS) for final acceptance email. Great job team, these steps will be our template for similar eu region brings. :tada:
